caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 304 of 2004
lawyer:
M.A. Azim, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Firoz Shah, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
For Respondents ----- Not represented.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Bangladesh Secretariat, Dhaka ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The First Court of Settlement, Bangladesh Abandoned Building, Segunbagicha, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 12. The statement made in paragraph-11 of the writ petition No. 5789 of 2003 which was filed challenging legality of the judgment of the 1st Court of Settlement dated 22.11.92 shows the state of play in the office of Attorney general, office of the Solicitor and in different Ministries which is of recent origin. In our view time is high for coming out of the state of play in filing case after inordinate delay upon making statement for condonation of delay which is nothing but got up story to shield latches, negligence and also cases of purposely making the case time barred. The Government, except in a case of highly exceptional nature, cannot have preferential treatment in the matter of condonation of limitation juxtaposition to the ordinary litigant and that the Government cannot have preferential treatment on the question of limitation in bulk number of case's, as is being noticed by us, since law of limitation equally applies to the Government as well as to the ordinary litigant. The present Civil Petition for leave to Appeal has been filed taking ground that Government machineries move slowly and as such time is consumed in taking decision and thus in the matter of delay while prayer for condonation is made by Government the same needs lenient consideration. The ground so taken merits not consideration since the explanation offered was found not sufficient and the delay was not sufficiently explained as was required by law. The other ground i.e. ground No. 2 is of no merit since the question as to whether the property was an abandon property or not was set at rest by the decree of title Suit No. 671 of 1985 and same having been maintained by this Court.
